why: A statement naming a script runs it; a call with arguments takes only a function (a script takes none: MATLAB doc 'Scripts vs. Functions', 'eval'; the case functions/script-vs-function-with-args). The statement takes the nearest file of the name, script or function, and a call with arguments the nearest function (project rule, the case functions/script-vs-function-with-args). The text `f; f(2); f(3);` holds three references of `f`, each placed where its name is written in the literal (project rule, step 14). So with a farther function `f.m` added the calls go to it and the statement stays on the script; with the script gone the statement goes to the function too; with the script back the statement runs it again: a real call, which a sync must not hide; and each step must end where a fresh index ends, counts included (project rule). Until step 14 the three were written where the text starts, and a sync lost the statement's reference once its edge met another's (found by the step 14 review).
